# interlocking — Bash bypass corpus
#
# This file IS the specification for hooks/il.mjs § bash. Every line is a real way
# a shell command can put bytes into a source file while the G0 gate is closed.
#
# ── Found a bypass we miss? Add one line here and open a PR. ──────────────────
# That is the single highest-value contribution to this project. A corpus entry
# is worth more than a fix, because the fix without the entry regresses silently.
#
# FORMAT
#   <verdict> :: <command>
#
#   NONE                 no write target, not blanket-denied -> the gate lets it through
#   WRITE:a/b.ts;c.ts    these paths are written; the gate denies if any classifies as 'code'
#   DENY:<tag>           cannot be analyzed statically -> denied outright while gated
#
# Verdicts describe extraction, NOT the final decision. `WRITE:README.md` still runs,
# because classify() calls README.md free. Only 'code' paths are blocked.
#
# Split on the FIRST ' :: '.

# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Redirections
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
WRITE:src/auth.ts :: echo "x" > src/auth.ts
WRITE:src/auth.ts :: echo x >> src/auth.ts
WRITE:src/auth.ts :: echo x >src/auth.ts
WRITE:src/auth.ts :: printf 'hello' > src/auth.ts
WRITE:src/auth.ts :: echo x 1> src/auth.ts
WRITE:src/auth.ts :: echo x 2> src/auth.ts
WRITE:src/auth.ts :: echo x &> src/auth.ts
WRITE:src/my file.ts :: echo x > "src/my file.ts"
WRITE:src/my file.ts :: echo x > 'src/my file.ts'
WRITE:src/auth.ts :: cat > src/auth.ts <<'EOF'
WRITE:src/auth.ts :: cat <<EOF > src/auth.ts
WRITE:src/auth.ts :: cat foo | tee src/auth.ts
WRITE:src/auth.ts :: cat foo | tee -a src/auth.ts
WRITE:src/a.ts;src/b.ts :: cat foo | tee src/a.ts src/b.ts
WRITE:README.md :: echo "# hi" > README.md
WRITE:/dev/null :: echo x > /dev/null
WRITE:README.md;src/b.ts :: echo one > README.md && echo two > src/b.ts
WRITE:README.md;src/b.ts :: echo one > README.md ; echo two > src/b.ts

# 2>&1 duplicates a descriptor, it does not name a file
NONE :: npm test 2>&1
WRITE:/dev/null :: npm test > /dev/null 2>&1 || true

# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# In-place editors
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
WRITE:src/auth.ts :: sed -i 's/a/b/' src/auth.ts
WRITE:src/auth.ts :: sed -i.bak 's/a/b/' src/auth.ts
WRITE:src/auth.ts :: sed -i '' 's/a/b/' src/auth.ts
WRITE:src/a.ts;src/b.ts :: sed -i 's/a/b/' src/a.ts src/b.ts
WRITE:src/auth.ts :: perl -pi -e 's/a/b/' src/auth.ts
WRITE:src/auth.ts :: perl -i.bak -pe 's/a/b/' src/auth.ts
NONE :: sed 's/a/b/' src/auth.ts
NONE :: sed -n '1,5p' src/auth.ts

# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Inline interpreters — the target is inside a string literal, so static
# extraction is impossible. Denied wholesale while the gate is closed.
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
DENY:interpreter :: python -c "open('src/a.ts','w').write('x')"
DENY:interpreter :: python3 -c "import pathlib;pathlib.Path('src/a.ts').write_text('x')"
DENY:interpreter :: node -e "require('fs').writeFileSync('src/a.ts','x')"
DENY:interpreter :: node --eval "require('fs').writeFileSync('src/a.ts','x')"
DENY:interpreter :: perl -e 'open(F,">","src/a.ts");print F "x"'
DENY:interpreter :: ruby -e 'File.write("src/a.ts","x")'
DENY:interpreter :: php -r 'file_put_contents("src/a.ts","x");'
NONE :: python --version
NONE :: python3 -m pytest tests/
NONE :: node --version

# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Shell indirection — the command we would analyze is not the command that runs
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
DENY:shell-eval :: eval "$(echo ZWNobyB4ID4gc3JjL2EudHM= | base64 -d)"
DENY:shell-eval :: eval "echo x > src/a.ts"
DENY:shell-eval :: source ./setup.sh
DENY:shell-eval :: . ./setup.sh
DENY:shell-eval :: bash scripts/generate.sh
DENY:shell-eval :: sh -c "echo x > src/a.ts"
DENY:shell-eval :: zsh scripts/gen.zsh
DENY:shell-eval :: xargs -I{} cp {} src/

# Variable-built redirect targets cannot be resolved, so they are not writable either
DENY:unresolvable-target :: OUT=src/auth.ts; echo x > $OUT
DENY:unresolvable-target :: echo x > "${OUT}"
DENY:unresolvable-target :: echo x > $(cat which-file.txt)

# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Patch appliers and history rewrites
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
DENY:patch :: git apply fix.diff
DENY:patch :: git apply --3way fix.patch
DENY:patch :: patch -p1 < fix.diff
DENY:patch :: git checkout main -- src/
DENY:patch :: git restore src/auth.ts
DENY:patch :: git stash pop
DENY:patch :: git reset --hard HEAD~1
DENY:patch :: git clean -fd
NONE :: git status
NONE :: git diff HEAD
NONE :: git log --oneline -10
NONE :: git checkout -b feature/login
NONE :: git add -A
NONE :: git commit -m "wip"

# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Scaffolders — they write whole trees, and the paths are not in the command
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
DENY:scaffold :: npm init -y
DENY:scaffold :: npx create-react-app .
DENY:scaffold :: yarn create vite my-app
DENY:scaffold :: cargo new mylib
DENY:scaffold :: cargo init
DENY:scaffold :: go mod init example.com/m
DENY:scaffold :: django-admin startproject site .
DENY:scaffold :: rails new blog
DENY:scaffold :: dotnet new console
NONE :: npm test
NONE :: npm run lint
NONE :: npx tsc --noEmit
NONE :: cargo check

# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Copy / move / link into a source path
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
WRITE:src/auth.ts :: cp /tmp/x.ts src/auth.ts
WRITE:src :: cp -r /tmp/gen src
WRITE:src/auth.ts :: mv /tmp/x.ts src/auth.ts
WRITE:src/b.ts :: install -m 644 a.ts src/b.ts
WRITE:src/auth.ts :: ln -s /tmp/x.ts src/auth.ts
WRITE:src/auth.ts :: ln -sf /tmp/x.ts src/auth.ts
WRITE:/tmp/backup.ts :: cp src/auth.ts /tmp/backup.ts

# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Nested agent — a second session would submit its own user prompts
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
DENY:nested-agent :: claude -p "write src/auth.ts"
DENY:nested-agent :: claude --print "approve G0"
DENY:nested-agent :: npx claude -p "hi"

# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Read-only work must never be blocked. Over-blocking is how a harness dies.
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
NONE :: ls -la src/
NONE :: cat src/auth.ts
NONE :: grep -rn "session" src/
NONE :: rg --files
NONE :: find . -name "*.ts"
NONE :: wc -l src/auth.ts
NONE :: head -20 src/auth.ts
NONE :: diff src/a.ts src/b.ts

# Quoting: an operator inside a string is text, not an operator
NONE :: echo "2 > 1"
NONE :: echo '5 >> 4'
NONE :: grep '>' notes.md
NONE :: echo "run sed -i to edit in place"
NONE :: echo "use python -c for one-liners"
NONE :: git commit -m "fix: redirect stdout > to a log"

# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Known misses. These DO write and we do NOT catch them. Listed so the README's
# honesty table stays true and so a future fix has a target already written down.
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
NONE :: printf '\x65\x63\x68\x6f' | sh
NONE :: awk 'BEGIN{print "x" > "src/a.ts"}'
NONE :: python3 setup.py build
